work.text: An original X post that satisfies a brand's campaign brief, by a creator ranked inside a curated influence map, whose hashed draft and later submission a miner platform commits on chain in hash-linked batches for validators to replay. Mechanism 0, the YouTube side in the repository the chain identity names, exists at about 2 percent of emission; this X side, mechanism 1, takes about 98 percent.
work.quote: This repository implements mechanism 1 of SN93 (~98% of subnet emission). The mechanism 0 YouTube creator-economy mechanism (~2% of emission)
work.disagrees: The chain identity and the index name bitcast-network/bitcast, the 2 percent YouTube repository, and the explainer treats YouTube as the work; the bitcast-x README and AGENTS.md fetched 2026-09-22 put X at about 98 percent, and no value in either repository's code or config fixes that split.

scoring.text: A language model passes or fails the post against the brief at temperature zero, any of three checks passing. A passing post's score starts at twice the author's influence in the campaign's curated map; each retweet from a listed account adds 1 times that account's influence, each quote 3 times, scaled by 0.1 + 0.9 / relationship score when the engager already has a tie to the author.

split.text: No value in code or config fixes the 98 to 2 split between the X and YouTube mechanisms; the validator submits only to mechid 1. At the default weight_score_blend of 1.0, a miner's weight is its share of deduplicated tweet scores. Dollar floors, daily campaign pools split by score to the 0.65 power, set weight only if the blend is lowered. No productive post, all weight burns to uid 0.
split.quote: Share of mechanism-1 emission weight allocated by deduplicated tweet scores instead of campaign floors. 1.0 (the default) allocates purely on content value
split.disagrees: docs/protocol.md at the same commit says reward construction sums per-tweet USD floors by miner UID and normalizes them into the weight vector; config.py defaults weight_score_blend to 1.0, which weights by tweet score and ignores floors unless lowered, and CHANGELOG.md lists the change under 3.0.0 as unreleased.

judges.text: Nine validators were active on the 2026-09-09 chain snapshot against five miners; commit-reveal is on. A validator re-derives the result: it reads each miner's 45-byte batch commitments from historical blocks, fetches the post and engagement from the X provider, runs the brief prompt on Chutes or OpenRouter, checks 15,000 alpha in conviction or stake, and submits to mechanism 1. Publisher, X provider and language model are not decentralized.
judges.quote: commit_reveal_weights_enabled True, weights_rate_limit 100; chain-2026-09-09.json active_validators 9, active_miners 5

cadence.text: Emission settles every 360 blocks, about 72 minutes. The validator polls every 12 seconds and submits weights once its mechanism 1 last update is older than weight_epoch_blocks, 100 by default. A campaign's reward pool pays over a seven-day emission window in daily budgets, and its featured post is pinned one day before close. A registration is immune from deregistration for 50,400 blocks, seven days.

buyer.text: Brands, none named. The dashboard on 2026-09-22 shows $438.1K lifetime revenue across chains, $276.7K of it spent buying the subnet token, and $544.0K paid to 1.3K creators, 78 on YouTube and 1,216 on X. The revenue ledger lists 1,211 transactions, USDC and USDT on Ethereum and TAO on the X side, with wallet addresses but no payer's name. No brand page, price for a brief, or contact.

exploits.text: Engagement rings: a retweet or quote from an account with an existing relationship score to the author is scaled by 0.1 + 0.9 / score, self-engagement is dropped, and creators passing the same brief cannot boost one another. Backdated attribution: the hashed draft must be committed on chain before the post exists, and a post counts once. Sybil miners: qualification needs 15,000 alpha in conviction or staked to the hotkey.
